name: sanity-e2e frontmatter
does: Declares the skill name
preventsClaim: unstated

name: sanity-e2e trigger description
does: Autonomous order-lifecycle smoke test, run before a PR or merge; no Firestore reads
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Assert only on operator surfaces
does: Every assertion lands on a WhatsApp reply, terminal UI, or tmux pane; throwaway phone per scenario; run autonomously
preventsClaim: a Firestore read confirms a document while the operator-visible surface is broken

name: Main agent orchestrates only
does: Never drive Playwright, never Read a screenshot; dev-up is invoked only here
preventsClaim: images are re-tokenized into this context every turn
costNote: the cost-control rule of the skill

name: P1 bring the stack up yourself
does: tmux check for 5 windows, run dev-up without asking, stop only on its error
preventsClaim: asking the user to do setup

name: P1b foreign stack human stop
does: Compare the firebase pane path to the repo root; stop and ask before taking over
preventsClaim: driving another worktree's functions/dist and hosting

name: P1c stale functions dist check
does: Compare newest dist mtime to the last functions/packages commit; rebuild on STALE_DIST
preventsClaim: validating a bundle 12 days old

name: P2 readiness markers
does: Abort with the offending pane tail unless all three markers are present
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Spawn the runner on sonnet
does: Runner subagent Reads runner.md itself; the spawn prompt spells out the resolved scenario selection and never inlines the runbook
preventsClaim: a subagent gets no slash-command variable expansion; inlining forfeits the whole token saving
costNote: 1 sonnet subagent driving a full order lifecycle

name: Relay the report unchanged
does: Pass through the per-scenario report and screenshot paths; never Read them
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Escalate the runner to opus
does: Bump from sonnet to opus when Sonnet fails a judgment point, and name it in the relay
preventsClaim: repeated escalations mean the default needs revisiting

name: Leave the stack up, relay verbatim
does: Reuse the stack; on a health problem run dev-up then dev-status before re-spawning
preventsClaim: unstated
costNote: avoids a stack restart per run

name: Runbook is self-contained
does: States the runner Reads this file into its own context and needs no other file
preventsClaim: the verbose runbook loading into the expensive main context
costNote: 233 lines that load only inside the runner subagent

name: Runner returns only the compact report
does: Drives WhatsApp and Playwright, no Firestore reads, returns the report plus screenshot paths
preventsClaim: a11y snapshots and pane captures reaching the main context

name: Scope excludes staff surfaces
does: Customer-business lifecycle only; /staff/** is ui-verify's job
preventsClaim: P3's owner guard would fail for a staff scenario

name: Runner config block
does: Owner credentials, restaurant, host URL, functions URL, test card, screenshot dir; create SHOT_DIR first
preventsClaim: a failure screenshot fails to save

name: P3 login and restaurant guard
does: Assert the terminal h2 contains Emulator Tacos, else abort
preventsClaim: running against the wrong seed or owner

name: P4 open-hours guard
does: Skip A-D inside the ~15-minute closed window and report closed window
preventsClaim: payment is unreachable inside the gap

name: P5 webhook delivery diagnosis
does: Sandbox pin is required; diagnose only if a paid order never reaches Nuevas; run D+E and report the gap if broken
preventsClaim: an unpinned command falls back to the live account; a broken listener hangs the run

name: Use the CLI forms as written
does: Read wa/SKILL.md as a CLI syntax reference only, never adopt its persona workflow
preventsClaim: personas would mutate the seeded customer set

name: H1 throwaway phone per scenario
does: Omit -f on the first text so the CLI generates a phone; reuse it
preventsClaim: re-runs collide and the seeded customer set mutates
costNote: one CLI call per scenario start

name: H2 baseline-diff pane wait
does: Poll the pane for new lines only; re-check with a phone-scoped grep before reporting a timeout failure
preventsClaim: a bare grep matches stale pane history; a saturated capture window degrades the baseline
costNote: polls every 2s up to 45s per wait

name: H3 bounded LLM retry
does: Retry the order text up to 3 times when Gemini times out
preventsClaim: a transient LLM timeout fails the scenario
costNote: up to 3 sends plus 3 waits per order

name: H4 extract the order id
does: First 20 chars after /pay/ in the reply
preventsClaim: unstated

name: H5 pick the right restaurant button
does: Choose the Emulator Tacos button id from the pane, not Pisca Cafe
preventsClaim: ordering from the wrong seeded restaurant

name: H6 tmux assertions
does: Payment landed, no transition error, expire dispatched, each read off a named pane
preventsClaim: unstated

name: H7 admin transition mechanics
does: Button-to-status map, two click blockers, re-login after Stripe, resolve fields from the snapshot, literal wait text
preventsClaim: an invented route renders 404 so the action silently never happens; an alternation wait can never match

name: H8 expire via curl
does: POST the expire-unconfirmed-order task directly
preventsClaim: the delayed task is never enqueued in the emulator

name: Scenarios are individually re-runnable
does: Each ends in a terminal state; single-scenario reruns supported
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Scenario A happy path
does: Place, pay through Stripe Checkout, accept, ready, picked-up, with capture proof
preventsClaim: money-before-state regression

name: Scenario B reject after payment
does: A1-A4 then Rechazar with a reason; assert the hold released
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Scenario C expire via curl
does: A1-A4 then H8; assert dispatch log, WA expire message, order off Nuevas
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Scenario D modify before paying
does: Re-quote with a higher subtotal, then cancel
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Scenario E routing and injection
does: Four one-line routing assertions including a prompt-injection text that must draw no reply
preventsClaim: the injection canary must stay silent by design
costNote: 4 fresh phones; one 30s timeout is expected

name: Runner report format
does: One line per scenario, screenshot paths, capture confirmable via logs, no Firestore reads, failure hints
preventsClaim: snapshots and pane captures crossing back to the main agent
costNote: the only bytes that leave the runner

name: sanity README not loaded at runtime
does: States only SKILL.md and runner.md load, and where operative steps belong
preventsClaim: rationale bloating a loaded file

name: Why the run happens in a subagent
does: Snapshots and pane captures accumulate and are re-billed every turn
preventsClaim: scenario E paying for every snapshot scenario A took

name: Two-actor table
does: Main agent owns P1/P2 and relay; runner owns guards, helpers, scenarios, report
preventsClaim: unstated
costNote: documentation; states the runner model as haiku while SKILL.md says sonnet

name: Why the runbook is a separate file
does: Progressive disclosure; inlining it forfeits the saving while looking identical
preventsClaim: a long runbook loading on every invocation

name: Why the prompt spells out the selection
does: A spawned subagent gets no slash-command variable expansion
preventsClaim: a runner that guesses or runs everything reads like a flaky skill

name: Why a cheap model runs it
does: The runbook is mechanical; bump on judgment-point failures
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Why P1/P2 stay with the main agent
does: Split by token profile; the stack is verified before paying to spawn a runner
preventsClaim: stack problems buried in a subagent report

name: Why assertions never touch Firestore
does: A Firestore read could confirm a document while the operator surface is broken
preventsClaim: unstated

name: wa frontmatter and trigger
does: Interact with the running WhatsApp emulator as simulated customers; manages personas
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Send and surface replies inline
does: Send through the wa-emulator CLI and echo the bot's replies; points at the chat viewer
preventsClaim: unstated

name: wa prerequisites
does: Requires dev-up's whatsapp window; resolves personas.json via a script
preventsClaim: running against a stack that is not up
costNote: stops and tells the user to run dev-up

name: personas.json shape and seeds
does: Six seeded personas covering Latin name, emoji, raw number, injection canary, short name
preventsClaim: unstated
costNote: 20 lines of JSON in the skill body

name: wa argument forms
does: Seven invocation shapes including persona management and tail
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Verify CLI flags at runtime
does: Run three --help calls before the first send and use the actual flag names
preventsClaim: the expected flag names may differ

name: Step 1 verify session and window
does: tmux check for the whatsapp window, else tell the user to run dev-up
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Step 2 load or scaffold personas
does: Resolve the live data dir, read or write personas.json, print the active persona
preventsClaim: unstated
costNote: one script run plus a read

name: Step 3 send then diff the pane
does: Invoke the matching CLI, sleep 2-3s, capture-pane diff, echo new bot lines
preventsClaim: the user misses the reply when not attached to the viewer
costNote: one CLI call plus one pane capture per send

name: Step 4 persona management
does: list, use, add (reject duplicate id), remove (warn when active)
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Step 5 tail the pane verbatim
does: Print the last N lines with no parsing
preventsClaim: unstated

name: Step 6 numbered interactive loop
does: Present eight numbered options and loop until the user picks 8
preventsClaim: unstated
costNote: blocks on the user every iteration

name: wa notes and constraints
does: Phone id shape, persona persistence, viewer is read-only, skill never reseeds; numbered prompts
preventsClaim: unstated
